parsedVerdict.reasoning: The Deliveryman domain model has real domain behaviour that belongs in the domain layer: the create factory, the addOrder limit invariant, the changeStatus guard and addNewMessageToOrders. However, the same class also defines how it is stored in the database, using TypeORM decorators. @Entity('deliverymans') sets the table name, @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') sets how ids are generated, @Column({ default: false }) sets a database default, and @OneToMany(..., { cascade: ['insert', 'update'] }) sets the relation mapping and cascade-save behaviour. Table names, column defaults, id generation and cascade rules are persistence responsibilities, which belong to the infrastructure layer. The rubric names persistence logic in a domain file as a failure. The import of typeorm is not part of this verdict, because import direction is out of scope. The misplaced responsibility is the persistence mapping that the decorators carry. Confidence is moderate because some projects deliberately accept ORM-annotated entities in the domain.

Move the ORM mapping into an infrastructure persistence entity or schema, and keep only the business behaviour in the domain model.
